meta.guide_tau: Level caption:  energy (NIST, or a measurement of the last 20 years where one exists) and measured lifetime (where one exists).
meta.notes: NIST ASD already carries A values for 166 Pt I lines; of the 58 measured lines (Gough-Hannaford-Lowe 1982, Lotrian-Guern 1982) in the Kurucz list gf7800.all only 3 are missing from NIST and those are added here (derived from log gf with A = 0.66702 sigma^2 gf / (2J'+1)). Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second); for the 248.792 nm line the heavier isotope lies at higher frequency. The 199Pt-198Pt shift on the same line is 0.98(48) GHz (199Pt is radioactive, not listed under isotopes). 195Pt has I = 1/2: hyperfine entries have A only. Isotope abundances in percent; abundance_unc in percent. Second pass (2026-10-02): 58 odd-level lifetimes from Den Hartog et al., Astrophys. J. 619, 639 (2005), Table 1 (levels there carry the Blaise et al. 1992 energies, matched to the NIST levels within 0.04 cm^-1 (most within 0.02) and by J). Where Table 2 prints an explicit uncertainty it is used; otherwise the uncertainty is the paper's stated rule 'larger of 5 % or 0.2 ns'. The NIST A values of Pt I already come from this paper's Table 3, so no transition rates were added. Third pass (2026-10-02): 195Pt hyperfine constants of 14 levels, isotope shifts of 11 lines and four g_J values from (a) the scanned CERN preprint of Neu et al. 1987 (pages read as images, Table 1 and Table 2 each read twice at two resolutions) and (b) the tables of LaBelle et al. 1989 embedded in Wayback copies of the Optica abstract page (parsed from the HTML, two captures identical). All were printed in mK (10^-3 cm^-1) and converted to MHz. Level names in those papers differ from NIST for the mixed J=2 even levels: paper '5d9 6s 3D2' = NIST 775.8761 (a 1D2), paper '5d8 6s2 3P2' = NIST 6567.4517 (3D2), paper '5d9 6s 1D2' = NIST 13496.2595 (b 1D2); paper '5d8 6s6p 5G5' = NIST 33680.39 (a 5F°5); paper '8_3' = NIST 37769.0673. The matching used the transition wavelengths and the printed g_J values. Isotope-shift keys follow nu(first) - nu(second): Neu values are stored as heavier-minus-lighter (negative), LaBelle values as nu(A) - nu(194). The lifetimes shown in Fig. 1 of the Neu preprint (130(3), 17.2(5), 14.0(3) ns) are the Gough et al. 1982 values already stored as alternatives.
